subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Hard-sell and soft-sell; discussing TV adverts; planning an evaluation / Writing an evaluation of an advertisement
outcomes: Explain the difference between hard-sell and soft-sell adverts
Sort positive and negative words for describing adverts
Write an evaluation of an advert with an opinion and reasons

tf.s: An advert must get its message across quickly.
tf.why: Yes, ads have very little time or space.

tf.s: A hard-sell advert focuses on how a product makes you feel.
tf.why: Hard-sell emphasises the product's features; soft-sell focuses on feelings.

tf.s: A soft-sell advert focuses on how a product makes consumers feel.
In advertising, 'copy' means the words in an advert.
tf.why: Right, copy is the text of the ad.

tf.s: 'Memorable' is a negative word for describing an advert.
tf.why: Memorable is positive: the ad is easy to remember.

tf.s: 'Repetitive' and 'misleading' are negative words for an advert.
tf.why: Yes, they describe bad points of an ad.

tf.s: An evaluation only describes the advert and gives no opinion.
tf.why: An evaluation must give your opinion supported by reasons.

tf.s: Many adverts combine hard-sell and soft-sell techniques.
tf.why: Yes, a car ad can show features and feelings.

tf.s: A washing machine ad that lists what the machine can do uses soft-sell.
tf.why: Listing features is a hard-sell technique.

tf.s: A second draft helps you correct mistakes and improve organisation.
tf.why: Correct, it makes your writing clearer.

boxes.why: Hard-sell tells you what the product can do.

o: how the product makes you feel

boxes.q: Which is a positive word for an advert?
Which is a negative word for an advert?

boxes.why: You give and support your view.

boxes.q: Why can an advert be irritating?
boxes.why: Seeing the same thing again and again annoys people.

o: an advert in a newspaper or magazine

boxes.why: A misleading ad makes you believe something untrue.

boxes.q: Where can you find help with the layout of an evaluation?
boxes.why: The Writing Guide shows structure and layout.

mcq.q: What is the main aim of an advertisement?
o: to get its message across quickly and persuade

mcq.q: Which list contains only positive words?
Which list contains only negative words?
What do you do after writing your first draft at school?
o: edit it at home and bring a second draft
mcq.why: A second draft improves your work.

mcq.q: An advert shows a family smiling happily in a car, with no technical details. Which technique is this?
mcq.why: It focuses on feelings, not features.

mcq.q: An advert lists a phone's camera, battery and memory. Which technique is this?
Which sentence gives an opinion with a reason?
o: In my opinion, the ad is misleading because it promises things the product can't do.
There is a shampoo in the ad.
mcq.why: It states a view and explains why.

mcq.q: Why do many car adverts combine hard-sell and soft-sell?
o: they show design features and also how driving the car feels
mcq.why: Combining both appeals to reason and emotion.

mcq.q: An advert repeats the same slogan many times. Why might viewers find it irritating?
o: it is repetitive and becomes annoying

mcq.q: Why is an evaluation more than a description?
o: it judges the ad and supports the judgement with reasons
mcq.why: Evaluating means giving and supporting your opinion.
